title: Project memory
description: Memory gives future coding tasks relevant guidance without replaying entire conversations. Workbench captures useful decisions and lessons; uncertain claims, conflicts, preferences and procedures need review.
manageDescription: Review proposals, correct entries and keep their revision history.
disabled: Project memory is off. Enable Self-improve under Project → Knowledge to capture or accept entries. Existing records remain viewable.
restartRequired: Workbench was updated while it was running. Restart the whole app to load project memory; reloading a window is not enough. Active workers keep running until you restart.
empty: No managed memories yet. Existing Markdown notes remain in the memory directory.
sourcePreview: Source preview shows the current file or task. The recorded evidence above is preserved with this revision.
proposalRecallHelp: Not used in task context yet. Accepting lets future workers receive this guidance when relevant; it does not verify tests or approve the source task.
proposalHelp: Describe when a future worker should act, what they should do, and why. Cite the evidence and any limits. Skip routine task recaps and facts already clear from the code. Corrections need acceptance again.
body: What should a future worker know, and why?
reference: Source reference (task id, project-relative file, or explicit instruction)
retention: Removing an entry stops future recall. Revision history and copies already recorded in task contexts or agent sessions remain. Legacy Markdown notes are preserved separately.
contextHelp: Exact context prepared for each task phase. This records what Workbench supplied, not whether the worker used it or whether its claims are true.
noContext: No recorded memory context for this task yet.
excerpt: Excerpt supplied; see the source for the full record.

kindHelp.decision: A project constraint and the reason for choosing it.
kindHelp.lesson: A specific trap encountered, what to do next time, and the evidence behind it.
kindHelp.procedure: When to use a validated process, its steps, and how to check the result. An implementation detail is not a procedure.
kindHelp.preference: An explicit standing instruction from you, with its intended scope.

verification.user-confirmed: Confirmed by a person; checks not independently verified
verification.source-backed: Source-backed: exact documentation quote checked in merged code; runtime claims not independently verified

disputed: Disputed by a pending proposal. Review the sources before relying on this claim.
